row: 600008 / AMR-005-0008 — GKT Problem 5.2 and Tabachnikov Section 7: null-chain closure on a Lorentz ellipsoid

Alper Ferudun, Explicit Rotation and Arithmetic Obstructions for Null Chains on a Lorentz Ellipsoid, v1.0, 14 October 2026. Theorem 1 gives the full analytic criterion for all positive real a,b,c: with f(t)^2=a sin^2(t)+b cos^2(t) and A=2 integral_0^(pi/2) f(t)/sqrt(c+f(t)^2) dt, k equator iterations with unreduced winding r close iff A=pi*k/(k+2r). Literal full tropic-to-tropic legs additionally require an even count; least periods and the unique positive c are included. Only this analytic theorem is accepted here; Theorem 2/Corollary 3 arithmetic and transcendence claims are not certified by this accounting audit. Publication postdates PR104 creation on 30 September 2026 and is current publication coverage, not evidence of antecedent priority. AI-assisted unrefereed preprint; PDF, source/support ZIP and README checksums verified. Existing publication; no new upload. https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/pull/104 .

row: 20000973 / AIM-COMBINATORICS-0098 — AIM 2013 Problem 8: critical-group torsors on spanning trees, minimum full-Aut(G)-equivariance formulation

Anonymous, An exact criterion for symmetry-respecting critical-group torsors, v0.2.0-candidate, 8 September 2026. Theorem 2.1 gives a complete necessary/sufficient finite criterion, class and actual-action counts, and construction of compatible simply transitive Jac(G)-actions on spanning trees using all subgroup marks and simultaneous H1 restriction kernels. Uses the actual induced Aut(G)-module action, with no chosen ribbon structure or sink. This answers the original explicit minimum; stronger unspecified naturality, unique canonical choice, minor consistency and efficient algorithms remain unestablished. row: 2104 / EP413 — Erdős 1979, p.71: infinitely many fixed-positive-epsilon barriers m+epsilon*omega(m)<=N for every positive m<N

Cheuk Fung (Joshua) Lau, On the Number of Prime Factors of Consecutive Integers, arXiv:2604.15042. Theorem 1.3 states Omega(n-k)<=C log k for infinitely many n and every 2<=k<n. Taking N=n-1 and epsilon=1/(C log 2) answers the full original fixed-positive-epsilon subquestion, since omega<=Omega and log(j+1)<=j log 2. The coefficient-one EP413 question remains unresolved by this record. PR1180 audited and repaired the inspected v2 (24 June 2026); current v3 (13 October 2026) was checked for statement/context, not re-certified in full and no v2 correction is silently transferred to it. The epsilon conclusion is independently supported by the reflected-weight application of Tao-Teräväinen, Quantitative correlations and some problems on prime factors of consecutive integers, arXiv:2512.01739v2 (25 April 2026), DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2512.01739, as documented in the accepted PR1180 review. One epsilon-result-family entry covers both sources; no new upload, first-priority claim or blanket certification of either whole paper. https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/pull/1180 .
